items.field: Stated objective/approach
items.value: Uses a theoretically-driven approach to interaction design to investigate the impact of different AR modalities in terms of information mode (video vs. 3D animation) and interaction modality (hand-gesture vs. voice command) on user performance, workload, eye gaze behaviours, and usability during a maintenance assembly task
items.quote: This paper uses a theoretically-driven approach to interaction design to investigate the impact of different AR modalities in terms of information mode (i.e. video vs. 3D animation) and interaction modality (i.e. hand-gesture vs. voice command) on user performance, workload, eye gaze behaviours, and usability during a maintenance assembly task.

items.field: Study design - procedure (consent, demographics, physiological sensor setup)
items.value: Participants read and signed a consent form approved by the Cranfield University Research Ethics System, filled an online demographic form (age, gender, maintenance experience, AR experience), and were equipped with an Empatica E4 wristband on the non-dominant hand.
items.quote: Prior to their participation, participants read and signed a consent form that was approved by the Cranfield University Research Ethics System. Before proceeding to the experiment session, an online form was filled in by the participant to collect demographic data such as age, gender, maintenance experience, and the experience with AR. Upon arrival, the participant was equipped with a wristband sensor (Empatica E4) to record their physiological responses.

items.value: How is AR task performance affected by different types of information mode (i.e. video vs. 3D animation) and interaction mode (i.e. hand gesture vs. voice command)?

items.field: Key result: completion time, 3D animation vs. video-based instruction

items.field: Key result: animation group participants noting misalignment of animation overlaid on the machine
items.value: three participants
items.quote: Only three participants noted the misalignment of the animation overlaid on the machine, yet still they admitted that the instructions were useful and understandable.

items.field: Key result: participants liking hand gesture interaction
items.value: 21 out of 21

items.field: Key result: voice group participants liking voice command
items.value: 20 out of 20

items.value: 38 out of 41

items.value: 7–8 min on average

items.field: Stated limitation: video-mode instruction required attention switching between video and mechanical component

items.field: Stated limitation: hand gesture fingertip positioning on button requires readjustment and multiple clicks
